use_cases.title: Submit a manuscript to a publishing package
use_cases.description: An author submits a book into a chosen publishing package by providing the book title, author name, email, genre, manuscript status, and one currently offered onboarding seat on the package detail page; the platform rejects missing required fields, rejects a missing manuscript-status choice, rejects stale or unoffered seats with explicit messages, suppresses the form entirely when the package is fully booked, and on success creates a `SUB-<n>` reference, confirms the claimed seat, and reduces the package’s remaining shared monthly capacity by one.
use_cases.summary: Submit a manuscript into a package.
use_cases.value: Captures publishing demand into a priced package while enforcing limited monthly onboarding capacity.

cite.quote:
An author must be able to submit a manuscript into a package, and must be told
clearly when the submission cannot be accepted.

cites.quote:
An author must be able to submit a manuscript into a package, and must be told
clearly when the submission cannot be accepted.

A valid submission returns to the package page and confirms with
  `Thanks, <author name> — "<book title>" has been submitted to the <package> package
  (<seat>). Reference: SUB-<n>. We'll be in touch within <n> business days.`

criteria.text: The submission form includes the core author and manuscript inputs, with default prompts for genre and manuscript status and an onboarding-seat select.

cite.quote: defaulting to `Select manuscript status`, and an onboarding seat select.

criteria.text: The manuscript-status select offers exactly `New Manuscript` and `Revised Manuscript`.

cite.quote: The manuscript status select offers exactly `New Manuscript` and `Revised Manuscript`.

criteria.text: The onboarding-seat select offers only seats still available this month.

cite.quote: The seat select offers only seats that are still available this month.

criteria.text: Submitting with any of book title, author name, email, or genre missing is rejected with `Please fill in the book title, author name, email, and genre.` and creates no submission.

cite.quote: Please fill in the book title, author name, email, and genre.

criteria.text: Submitting without choosing a manuscript status is rejected with `Please select whether this is a new or revised manuscript.`

cite.quote: Please select whether this is a new or revised manuscript.

criteria.text: Submitting with a seat that is already taken, or not offered, is rejected with `That seat is no longer available this month. Please choose another.`

cite.quote: That seat is no longer available this month. Please choose another.

criteria.text: A valid submission confirms the author, book title, package, seat, `SUB-<n>` reference, and turnaround window.

cite.quote: dropped by one.

use_cases.title: Compare publishing packages and seat availability
use_cases.description: An author reviews the publishing packages on `/publish` and on each package detail page to compare package names, taglines, prices, turnaround times, features, package codes, and remaining onboarding seats from the shared monthly pool; the flow distinguishes available packages from fully booked ones, exposes the exact capacity messaging, and returns a 404 when a nonexistent package is requested.
use_cases.summary: Compare packages and current seat availability.
use_cases.value: Helps authors choose the right paid publishing package before scarce onboarding seats are claimed.

cite.quote:
Authors must be able to compare packages and see how much onboarding capacity is
left this month.

cites.quote:
Authors must be able to compare packages and see how much onboarding capacity is
left this month.

**Seats are a shared, global monthly pool.** A seat claimed by any visitor is gone
  for every visitor until it is withdrawn; the pool only resets when the app
  restarts. Submissions themselves are per-browser-session.
  Starter has 6 seats, Standard 4, Premium 2 and Author's Choice exactly 1.

criteria.text: `/publish` lists exactly four named packages with fixed package pricing and turnaround values.

cite.quote: Standard ($999, 30-day), Premium ($1999, 21-day) and Author's Choice ($3499, 14-day).

use_cases.title: Track and withdraw a manuscript submission
use_cases.description: An author views the submissions currently held for that browser session, sees each submission’s reference, book title, author, package, seat, and status, and can withdraw a submission to remove it from the table, restore the claimed onboarding seat to the shared monthly pool, and keep the `My Submissions (N)` header count aligned with the current session state.
use_cases.value: Gives authors self-serve visibility into current submissions and a way to release scarce seat capacity.

cite.quote: An author must be able to see what they have submitted and take it back.

cites.quote: An author must be able to see what they have submitted and take it back.

criteria.text: With nothing submitted, `/my-submissions` shows `You haven't submitted a manuscript yet.` and links the user back to browse packages.

cite.quote: `You haven't submitted a manuscript yet.` and a link to browse packages.

cite.quote: A new submission's status is `Under Review`.

cite.quote: The header `My Submissions (N)` count matches the number of rows in the table.

criteria.text: Each submission row offers a `Withdraw` control that removes that row from the table.

cite.quote: Each row offers a `Withdraw` control that removes that row from the table.

criteria.text: Withdrawing a submission returns its seat to the pool, so the package’s remaining seat count on `/publish` goes back up by one.

cite.quote: Submissions themselves are per-browser-session.

use_cases.title: Search the published-books catalog
use_cases.description: Any visitor searches from the header search box to open a shareable `/search` results page for the entered term, with matching performed case-insensitively across titles, authors, and genres; results use the same core book-tile information as the catalog, exact title searches can narrow to a single known book, and unmatched or blank searches resolve to the same explicit no-results message instead of an empty or broken page.
use_cases.summary: Search published books from the header.
use_cases.value: Helps readers reach relevant published books quickly from anywhere in the site.

cite.quote: Anyone must be able to find a published book from the header search box.

cites.quote: Anyone must be able to find a published book from the header search box.

Searching sends the term to `/search` as a shareable URL carrying the term, and
  the results page is headed `Search results for "<term>"`.
- A term that matches a title returns that book — searching `The Iron Court`
  returns exactly one result, `The Iron Court` by `Branwen Oduya`.
- Matching is case-insensitive: a lower-case term returns the same results as the
  same term upper-cased.
- A term is matched against title, author **and** genre, so searching a genre name
  such as `Mystery` returns that genre's books.

criteria.text: Searching sends the term to `/search` as a shareable URL carrying the term, and the results page is headed `Search results for "<term>"`.

cite.quote: the results page is headed `Search results for "<term>"`.

cite.quote: such as `Mystery` returns that genre's books.
